items.text: Overnight into 20 November Russia launched one of its largest combined air attacks of the war: Ukraine's Air Force counted 84 cruise missiles and 404 drones, and [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] cited 27 more ballistic missiles. Kyiv mayor [[p:Vitali Klitschko]] said three Dnipro bridges were damaged. At least eight people were killed, and nuclear plants cut output, causing outages in Kyiv and 10 regions. Russia's Defence Ministry said it hit bridges used to move weapons, a day after [[p:Vladimir Putin]] vowed retaliation for Ukraine's strike on the Crimean Bridge.
items.reporter: Abbey Fenbert, Dmytro Basmat, Volodymyr Ivanyshyn
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Tolls differ: Al Jazeera/Reuters 8 killed, Kyiv Independent at least 9. A further wave (3 ballistic missiles, 148 drones) came overnight 20–21 Nov.

items.text: Poland says two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone came down on its territory during the overnight attack on Ukraine, with no injuries. PM [[p:Donald Tusk]] called it an apparently intentional provocation and Warsaw asked NATO for AWACS aircraft and F-35s. NATO Secretary General [[p:Mark Rutte]] called the incident clearly dangerous; Tusk said Rutte would visit Warsaw on 21 Nov.
items.notes: Kyiv Independent identifies the missiles as Kh-101s. No Russian response quoted.

items.text: UK Maritime Trade Operations reported two incidents of tankers hit by unidentified projectiles near Khasab, Oman, on 21 Nov, possibly involving the same ship; no casualties were reported. They follow a 20 Nov strike that set a tanker on fire in the same area. Iran's [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|Revolutionary Guards]] claimed to have shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the strait, which is unconfirmed.
items.notes: Same day the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh (Al Jazeera live page).

items.text: The [[e:COP31|2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] in Antalya overran its 20 Nov close without a final package. A night session adopted decisions including on Paris Agreement carbon markets and confirmed Ethiopia will host COP32. Finance, mitigation, adaptation and the just transition remain open; COP31 president [[p:Murat Kurum]] said a third draft was due on 21 Nov. France, Panama and others objected to an earlier draft that dropped fossil fuels.
items.notes: Link2 is AFP via Manila Times. Update if a final text is adopted.

items.text: The military's [[p:ISPR|Inter-Services Public Relations]] said four soldiers, including a major, and 24 militants were killed in Balochistan and North Waziristan. Two soldiers died when armed quadcopters hit a patrol at Kardagap in Mastung; Pakistan blamed Baloch separatists and again accused India of backing them, which India denies. In North Waziristan the military said 16 militants, two of them Afghan, were killed.
items.notes: Soldiers' deaths confirmed by the military; militant tolls are ISPR's alone. Dawn corrected an N. Waziristan toll from 14 to 16.

items.text: The [[p:Balochistan Liberation Army]] said its drone unit carried out four attacks in Mastung and Kalat between 5 and 14 Nov, killing six security personnel, and released video of the 14 Nov Kardagap strike. Pakistan has confirmed two deaths, both from 14 Nov.
items.notes: Only the 14 Nov attack matches Pakistan's own confirmation; the rest is unverified.

items.text: Security sources said Frontier Corps troops killed two armed men near the Quetta–Taftan highway in Chagai who they said were scouting Dalbandin airport. Officials linked them to the BLA and denied that the airport was attacked.
items.notes: Unnamed security sources only.

items.text: The military said it killed 22 militants in 48 hours of raids in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (15 in South Waziristan, six in Bannu, one in Tank), calling them India-sponsored; its term covers the Pakistani Taliban.
items.notes: Military figures only; AP carried them without independent verification.

items.text: Gunmen killed two police officers in Bannu within 24 hours; one was abducted and found tortured to death. In Lakki Marwat police said four Pakistani Taliban fighters died in a two-hour gunfight.
items.outlet: The Express Tribune / Arab News Pakistan
items.notes: No claim for the Bannu killings.

items.text: Pakistan hosted the 30th ministerial council of the [[p:Economic Cooperation Organization]] in Islamabad and took the bloc's chair, without inviting Afghanistan. The Foreign Office said Pakistan does not recognise the Taliban government and Afghanistan's membership of the secretariat is suspended. It also rejected Indian remarks at the UN Security Council and repeated its claim that India backs militants.
items.outlet: Associated Press of Pakistan / Arab News Pakistan
items.notes: AP separately confirmed Afghanistan's absence. India denies backing militancy.

items.text: Foreign Minister [[p:Ishaq Dar]] said Pakistan is waiting for a US reply to Iran's latest proposals and that Iran has cut its proposed timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz from seven days to two. Iran's [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] met army chief [[p:Asim Munir]] in Islamabad, and the ECO communiqué endorsed Pakistani and Qatari mediation.
items.notes: Sources differ on the date and name of the June interim deal. No US response reported.

items.text: The [[p:Islamabad High Court]] resumed appeals by [[p:Imran Khan]] and [[p:Bushra Bibi]] against their Al-Qadir Trust convictions. Khan's lawyer said he had not met his client in seven months and that Khan's blood pressure was uncontrolled; the court ordered a lawyers' meeting within two days. The appeals are listed for 25 Nov.
items.notes: Reports differ on how long the defence was given to prepare.

items.text: The [[p:State Bank of Pakistan]]'s annual report said inflation reached double digits from April after the oil shock from the Middle East war; reserves beat the $18bn end-June target. Pakistan expects IMF board approval of a $1.2bn tranche in early December.
items.notes: IMF date (possibly 9 Dec) from earlier Dawn reporting.

items.text: Taliban leader [[p:Hibatullah Akhundzada]], who rarely leaves Kandahar, spoke at a conference on his decrees at [[p:Kabul University]] under heavy security, with media barred. AFP reports he said religious education matters more than modern education (translated from French). Taliban sources told Afghanistan International the visit aimed to contain rifts, including with Interior Minister [[p:Sirajuddin Haqqani]].
items.notes: Rift claims rest on unnamed sources.

items.text: A Taliban deputy health minister said Kabul signed a deal with Iran to supply medicines. Shortages have followed the Taliban's February ban on imports from Pakistan, which supplied over 70% of Afghanistan's medicines.
Sources told Afghanistan International the Taliban freed two Shia clerics in Herat after two days in detention, reportedly on condition they give up mourning ceremonies.
items.notes: Only the summary was readable.

items.text: Afghanistan marked 80 years of UN membership with its seat still held by an envoy of the former republic; the Taliban called the refusal an injustice.

Uzbek and Afghan railway authorities agreed to run freight from Hairatan to Mazar-i-Sharif. Uzbekistan's water minister said the Qosh Tepa canal has not yet drawn Amu Darya water and future withdrawals must be negotiated.
UNHCR and IOM data show Pakistan arrested 796 Afghans in the first week of November, mostly in Balochistan; 4,662 Afghans went home that week, 809 of them deported.

Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said an interim India–US trade deal is more or less final but cannot be signed until Washington sets its new tariff framework, after the US Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs. India aims to bring its EU free trade agreement into force in early 2027.

India and Pakistan clashed over the suspended [[p:Indus Waters Treaty]] at a UN Security Council meeting; Pakistan cited an August arbitration award saying the treaty remains in force. As Pakistan's climate minister arrived in Delhi for an SCO forum on 20 Nov, India's foreign ministry said there was no change in its position.
items.notes: Each side's account comes through its own outlets.

items.text: A Manhattan federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison for the foiled plot to kill Sikh separatist [[p:Gurpatwant Singh Pannun]]. US prosecutors allege a former Indian intelligence officer recruited Gupta; India says that officer no longer works for the government.
items.notes: No Indian government reaction reported.

items.text: [[p:S. Jaishankar]] and [[p:Rajnath Singh]] held the fourth India–Japan 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo on economic security, supply chains and maritime chokepoints; no specific agreements were announced.
Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha and weakened; about 372,000 people were moved to shelters and the state reported no major damage or deaths.
Security forces killed a suspected [[p:Kangleipak Communist Party]] faction militant in a gunfight in Imphal West, Manipur; regional reports said eight were detained.
A gunfight broke out in Kulgam, south Kashmir, during a search operation after an 11 Nov attack on CRPF personnel; police gave no casualty details.
items.notes: Reports of a militant killed are unconfirmed.

items.text: A US congressional panel, the [[p:United States–China Economic and Security Review Commission]], said growing Chinese military support for Pakistan makes a two-front scenario a pressing concern for India.

A nationwide lockdown called by the banned [[p:Awami League]] on the anniversary of [[p:Sheikh Hasina]]'s death sentence brought arson in at least 12 districts, including police stations in Gopalganj, Grameen Bank branches and the Chattogram family home of [[p:Muhammad Yunus]]. AFP reports at least three dead. Dhaka police said 773 people were arrested in two days of operations.
items.notes: Tolls differ: AFP 3, Dhaka Tribune 4; Prothom Alo reports two BNP activists beaten to death in Narail (https://www.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/district/o7q13sktek). Grameen Bank says 72 offices attacked 10–19 Nov.

items.text: Bangladesh's law minister said Dhaka has completed every legal step to seek Sheikh Hasina's extradition and the decision rests with India, which calls it a legal matter. Hasina, sentenced to death in absentia, has said she plans to return in December.

Bangladesh asked India for talks on renewing the 1996 Ganges Water Treaty, which expires on 12 Dec. An Indian team is in Dhaka on 21–23 Nov for the Joint Rivers Committee, but Indian sources told ThePrint renewal is not on the agenda.
Parliament passed the second reading of President [[p:Anura Kumara Dissanayake]]'s 2027 budget by 157 votes to 60. The committee stage starts on 21 Nov and the final vote is on 14 Dec.
items.notes: Daily Mirror states a majority of 98 but its tally gives 97, as Newswire reports. Closes W-261114-02.

items.text: The [[p:Central Bank of Sri Lanka]] unexpectedly raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 9% and lifted the reserve ratio to 3%, citing 8.3% inflation, energy prices from the Middle East war and rupee weakness.
Teachers' and principals' unions plan a black protest on 23 Nov over pay anomalies; a minister pointed them to a salaries commission due to report by June 2027.

PM [[p:Balen Shah]] will make his first official visit to India on 22–23 Nov at [[p:Narendra Modi]]'s invitation, with MoUs on education, health and disaster management to be exchanged. Unnamed Nepali officials say India responded positively to a request for about $2bn in loans and grants.
items.notes: $2bn figure from unnamed sources; both links same outlet.

items.text: The Supreme Court ordered the government to explain why it removed police chief Dan Bahadur Karki on 4 Nov but refused to reinstate him in the meantime; the next hearing is on 23 Nov.
Former president [[p:Bidya Devi Bhandari]] told a CPN-UML gathering that the Shah government is targeting opponents and the media.

Parliament sent four government bills to committee, including the Real Estate Development Bill underpinning the Ras Malé project, passed 42–13 over opposition votes. [[p:Mohamed Nasheed]] of the [[p:Maldivian Democratic Party]] called for a referendum on giving 500 hectares of Ras Malé to UAE developer Eagle Hills; President [[p:Mohamed Muizzu]] rejected it.
items.notes: Dates inferred; Atoll Times shows relative dates. Budget Committee passed the MVR 59.7bn 2027 budget on 19 Nov (Edition.mv).

items.text: Bhutan extended the halved Sustainable Development Fee for tourists ($100 a night) until December 2029.

[[p:Nikol Pashinyan]] said he would resign if voters reject a new constitution in a referendum, and would not run for PM again once the peace treaty with Azerbaijan is ratified if they approve it. He said a preliminary draft would be published next week and suggested early elections if the opposition blocks the vote; his party has 64 of the 70 seats needed to call a referendum.
items.notes: Azerbaijan makes constitutional change a precondition for signing the treaty. Eurasianet gives the seat arithmetic.

items.text: Azerbaijan's [[p:Jeyhun Bayramov]], hosting Germany's [[p:Johann Wadephul]], said the technical parameters of the US-backed TRIPP route through Armenia must be agreed with Baku, since its entry and exit points are on Azerbaijan's border. A joint technical group began work on 6 Nov, he said.

An Armenian–Russian working group held its first meeting on revising the concession under which a [[p:Russian Railways]] subsidiary runs Armenia's network until 2038. Yerevan says sanctions on Russian firms and lack of investment hurt Armenia's competitiveness.

The [[p:Constitutional Court of Georgia]] continued hearing [[p:Georgian Dream]]'s suit to ban five opposition parties and rejected a motion to set evidence standards before ruling. The Public Defender filed an opinion that criticising the government is not grounds for a ban. The court has until 24 June 2027 to rule.
items.notes: Only the JAMnews digest found for 17–18 Nov; needs cross-check.

items.text: A Tbilisi court sentenced Eliso Kiladze, founder of the regional outlet Khronika+, to 10 years for fraud and money laundering in a closed trial. She says she is innocent and the case is revenge by a former security chief; she plans to appeal.

PM [[p:Irakli Kobakhidze]] said Georgia's new special representative for Russia will soon meet Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin, while ruling out full diplomatic ties while Russia occupies Abkhazia and Tskhinvali. The opposition called a nationwide rally for 28 Nov.
A gas explosion destroyed part of an apartment block in Tbilisi's Ponichala district, killing six, including two young girls; 22 Nov was declared a day of mourning.

Parliament took up NGO-law amendments requiring local and foreign NGOs to re-register within 30 days and letting the executive suspend groups for up to a year without a court order. Lawyers quoted by JAMnews say the bill moves decisions from courts to officials.
items.notes: No final vote reported yet.

items.text: A leak investigation reported that [[p:Deutsche Bank]] flagged over $3m in payments to companies behind the unbuilt Trump tower in Baku as suspicious, one linked to the Azerbaijani Laundromat.
items.notes: JAMnews summary of the iStories consortium work.

items.text: A court approved pre-trial arrest for the heads of the wealth fund and state railway. President [[p:Kassym-Jomart Tokayev]] called the case a sign of widespread corruption in state companies and ordered anti-corruption proposals by 24 Nov.

Uzbek professor Ikboljon Koraboyev, who taught in Astana, was reportedly sentenced to 10 years for espionage in a closed trial; colleagues say his critical-minerals research used open sources. Neither government has commented.
items.notes: Verdict date not stated.

items.text: Iskhak Masaliev became the fourth presidential hopeful, after President [[p:Sadyr Japarov]], to pass the 30,000-signature threshold for the 27 Jan election.

Businessman Kubat Alymbekov accused security officials of seizing his Issyk-Kul resort and blamed the president's brother; Japarov denied any family stake and the security service said a Russian investor received the company as compensation in a criminal case.
The government gave state-owned ElKat, 51% owned by the presidential administration, an indefinite monopoly on international internet traffic. Critics warn of higher prices and easier blocking.

Putin held talks in Dushanbe with [[p:Emomali Rahmon]] on labour migration, security and Russia's [[p:201st Military Base]]; no agreements were reported. The visit followed EU sanctions on Unistream, a Russian bank widely used for migrant remittances.

Rahmon met US Deputy Secretary of State [[p:Christopher Landau]] on mining, investment and counter-terrorism; Tajikistan produces about a fifth of the world's antimony, until now exported to China. No deals were announced.

Citing The New York Times, Kursiv reported that a Russian paper on ending the Ukraine war, handed to US negotiators, asks NATO to halt military activity in Central Asia and the South Caucasus. Regional governments were not consulted and have not reacted.
items.notes: Unsigned negotiating document; Moscow has not confirmed it.

items.text: During [[p:Shavkat Mirziyoyev]]'s visit to Muscat, Uzbekistan and Oman upgraded ties to a strategic partnership and signed over 30 documents, including visa exemption.
Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are preparing a World Bank-backed shared electricity market, with first trades possible in 2028–29.
President Serdar Berdimuhamedov sent the draft 2027 budget to parliament.
